No, not all of it. Of the roughly 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss mapped in 2021, the MGAP 2021 forest map places about 68.1 ha (around 84%) in planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. The other 13.2 ha lies outside mapped forest, and none of it is native forest. The area figures are rounded, so the split is approximate.

Two caveats:
- Another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event, so it isn't in the 81.3 ha or the split above.
- The forest map gives territorial context only. It doesn't show what caused the loss. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as plantation harvest, so this doesn't establish deforestation, cause, legality, or compliance.
